title: Privacy Policy
summary: Draft for owner review. It describes the current staging service and the checks still needed before admitting real users.

blocks.text: This policy is a draft. It has not been approved, has no effective date, and is not a final privacy notice. Reading it, following a link to it, or using Dayli does not record acceptance. Dayli must not present it as the final policy until the operator, processing details, retention practice, and final wording have been approved.

Dayli is operated by agroupforcoders, an informal group based in New Zealand, not a registered company. The owner personally monitors agroupforcoders@gmail.com for privacy, access, correction, under-16, security, and deletion requests. Delivery to that inbox and an absence arrangement still need a live check before public registration.

The planned public service is available worldwide to people aged 16 and over. Public registration requires an explicit, initially unchecked 16+ declaration and acceptance of the effective Terms. The current documents remain drafts; neither their display nor a prior sign-in establishes that acceptance. Dayli does not ask for a birth date or identity document by default. Report a possible under-16 account by email for an individual review and appeal, not automatic deletion.

To create and run an account, Dayli handles your username, public name if you provide one, email address, account identifier, password hash, account and session records, session IP address, user agent, verification and password-recovery records, and rate-limit records. Dayli does not store passwords as plaintext.

Dayli supports email and password accounts. Google sign-in may be available when it is enabled for the deployment. A Google identity is not linked to an existing Dayli account only because the email addresses match. Where configured, Resend sends password-recovery and verification emails.

Dayli handles the journal content and social information needed for its features. This includes posts, captions, ratings, optional weather condition, temperature and place name, tomorrow notes, audiences, release times, revisions, friendships, friend requests, blocks, direct messages, message edits, message reactions, and message-request decisions. Earlier post revisions can remain stored when a post is edited. Dayli does not store coordinates for the optional weather snapshot.

The mobile app stores a bearer session, cached identity, and unsent drafts in protected device storage. Media selected in the current web and mobile composer stays on the device and is not posted yet. If push notifications are enabled, Dayli handles a device registration token. Notification payloads are designed to identify a conversation without message text.

Dayli uses account and session information to sign people in, protect accounts, recover passwords, apply rate limits, and operate available features. It uses posts, friendships, and blocks to decide who can view a post. It uses direct-message information to deliver and display messages to the people in a conversation. It uses device registration information to send notifications when that feature is enabled.
Dayli does not use personal content for research or to train AI systems. Content is server-readable, so this is not end-to-end encrypted messaging or journaling.

Solo and unreleased posts are for their author. A released friends-audience post from a public account can be read by anyone, including a visitor without an account. On a private account, active friends can read released friends-audience posts. Direct messages are available to conversation participants under the current access rules. Blocking limits future access for the affected signed-in accounts, but cannot take back information someone already saw, copied, or saved.

Dayli uses Neon PostgreSQL for application data and Cloudflare services for storage and application delivery. Depending on configuration, Google may process sign-in, Firebase may deliver mobile push, and Resend may process authentication email. If a person chooses weather by location in the mobile composer, their phone sends the approximate location to Open-Meteo and its own geocoder to obtain weather and a place name. If they search for a place, the search and weather request go to Open-Meteo. Only the resulting condition, temperature, and place name are sent to Dayli with the post. The operator has not verified the location of every copy, log, recovery operation, or provider process. This draft does not promise storage or processing in any one region.

The operator reports using only Cloudflare-provided analytics. The enabled analytics products, identifiers, logs, purposes, and retention settings have not yet been inventoried. This draft therefore does not claim that Dayli has no analytics or tracking.

Account content may be retained indefinitely while no verified account-deletion process is operating. Provider recovery copies, recovery history, object versions, and log-retention settings remain unverified. The planned 7-day cancellation, 14-day active cleanup, and 30-day backup expiry are not live promises. Dayli does not use a backup to selectively restore content you deleted, but this draft does not promise that every provider recovery copy has expired.

Signed-in staging users can request one owner-scoped, versioned ZIP export from /account/export. When ready, its authenticated download remains available for 24 hours unless account access ends sooner. The archive includes approved owned records and may exclude received message bodies and other people's private data; it is not a full response to every formal access request. Dayli does not yet provide verified account deletion or physical purge. Contact agroupforcoders@gmail.com about access, correction, or deletion. The operator will review requests under applicable law, but email does not trigger an automated deletion process, and this draft cannot claim that removal is currently available.

Dayli uses access controls and secure session handling, but no system can guarantee absolute security. The operator approves policy changes and normally gives 30 days of notice for material Terms changes. An urgent shorter period requires an explained notice. This draft is not a final privacy notice or a statement that public registration is ready.
